name: Omid Drug Rehabilitation Center, Kabul
detail: Pakistani F-16 strike on March 16, 2026 targeting the Omid center in Kabul's Khair Khana district. Pakistan claimed the facility harbored TTP militants; Afghan and UN investigators found no evidence. Revised toll: 411 killed, 263 injured — mostly patients. HRW declared the strike unlawful.

name: Sarkano and Narai Districts, Kunar Province
detail: Pakistan fired 85 artillery shells into Kunar province on March 25, 2026, following expiry of the Eid ceasefire. Targets included Sarkano (47 shells + 2 drone strikes), Narai, Manura (2 shells), Shultan (15 shells), and Asadabad surroundings (5 shells). 2 civilians killed, 8 wounded.

name: TTP Positions — Paktika, Khost, Nangarhar Provinces
detail: Operation Ghazab-il-Haq targeting of alleged TTP and militant infrastructure across Paktika, Khost, and Nangarhar provinces following resumption of operations on March 26, 2026. Pakistan claims 62 locations struck since February 26, 237 outposts destroyed. Casualty figures disputed.

name: Dangam District, Kunar Province — Civilian Areas (May 5, 2026)
detail: Pakistani military strikes hit Dangam district in northern Kunar province on May 5, 2026, killing 3 civilians and injuring 14. Targets reportedly included residential homes, a school, a health centre, and a mosque. Afghanistan called the strike a 'war crime' and demanded UN Security Council action. Pakistan denied civilian casualties. Part of Op Ghazab lil-Haq's continued strikes on eastern Afghan provinces.

name: Khost, Kunar & Paktika Provinces — Op Ghazab Resumption (Jun 10, 2026)
detail: Pakistan's first confirmed cross-border strikes since the May 5 Dangam strike, hitting a training centre, hideout, ammunition cache, and TTP commander-linked sites across Khost, Kunar, and Paktika. Pakistan claims 26 militants killed; Taliban says 13 civilians killed including 11 children. Triggered by the June 9 Musa Dara FC-post attack, ending a 35-day operational pause.

name: Chamkani, Gyan & Marawara Districts — Largest Strikes Since Pause (Jun 28-29, 2026)
detail: Pakistan's largest Operation Ghazab lil-Haq strikes since the pause ended, hitting Chamkani (Paktia), Gyan (Paktika), and Marawara (Kunar) in retaliation for the June 27 Karachi Rangers camp attack. UNAMA confirmed 28 civilians killed and 49 injured; Taliban officials cite 36 killed and ~160 wounded; Pakistan claims 25-29 militants killed. Accompanied by a Bajaur ground operation killing 4 militants including a senior Jamaat-ul-Ahrar commander.
